recommendations.headline: Call satisfaction is the single biggest predictor of a sale (72% win rate when satisfied vs 15% neutral and 8% dissatisfied), yet 44% of calls stay only 'neutral' and reps consistently skip basic closing steps (201 calls with no fixed follow-up, 128 with no quote sent, 107 where the order wasn't even asked for) — fixing call execution, not price, is the fastest lever to raise the 20% overall order rate.
behaviour: Customers are heavily price-driven and comparison-shopping: price_shopper (218) and comparing_quotes (146) are top behaviours, alongside repeat_buyer (126) and bulk_buyer (122) showing a mixed transactional/relationship base.
744 of 1584 calls (47%) end in 'callback' rather than a clear yes/no, the single largest outcome bucket, showing stalling behaviour rather than outright rejection.
Price is raised often but rarely resolved: price_reaction shows 949 calls (60%) 'not_discussed', only 141 'accepted' and 198 'negotiating' — many conversations never get to a firm price position.

Stock_availability (211 calls) and price_high (208 calls) are the top two objections, but stock objections convert worst (25% win) even below price objections (28% win), meaning availability is hurting sales more than price itself.

Dealers are the largest segment (811 calls, 51%) with a 39% win rate, but the 'unknown' segment (519 calls, 33%) wins only 26% — reps are often not capturing who they're talking to or what they need (didnt_ask_requirement flagged 54 times).
satisfaction: Satisfaction strongly predicts sales: satisfied calls win 72% of the time vs 15% for neutral and 8% for dissatisfied calls — satisfaction, not price, separates winners from losers.
Only 471 of 1584 calls (30%) are rated satisfied; 702 (44%) are merely neutral — a large pool of calls that could convert much better with small service improvements.

Price-high is a top objection (208 calls, 13% of all calls) but even these calls still convert at 28% when handled well, showing price alone isn't the main blocker — execution is (slow/unclear answers flagged 214 times).
Dissatisfaction is rare (115 calls, 7%) but devastating — only 8% of these convert, confirming a few bad experiences cost disproportionately more than price objections do.

conversion.title: Enforce the 3-step call close (quote, order ask, fixed follow-up)
conversion.evidence: rep_missed shows no_follow_up_fixed in 201 calls, no_quote_sent in 128, and didnt_ask_for_order in 107 — all basic, fixable steps.
conversion.action: Mandate every call ends with: a quote sent the same day, an explicit order ask, and a specific callback date/time logged in CRM.

conversion.title: Systematically work the 744-call callback backlog
conversion.evidence: Callback is the largest outcome (744 calls, 47%) vs only 320 orders (20%) — most 'maybes' are never chased to closure.
conversion.action: Assign each callback an owner and SLA (e.g., contact within 24-48h); review weekly in team meetings to push callbacks to order or close as not_interested.

conversion.title: Raise call quality to shift neutral calls to satisfied
conversion.evidence: Neutral calls (702, 44%) win only 15% vs 72% for satisfied; slow_or_unclear_answer flagged 214 times.
conversion.action: Coach reps on quick, confident, accurate answers (rates, specs, stock) within the call; use call scripts/cheat-sheets for common SKUs to cut hesitation.

conversion.title: Fix stock-availability objection handling
conversion.evidence: Stock_availability is the top objection (211 calls) with the lowest win rate (25%), and didnt_offer_alternative flagged 71 times.
conversion.action: Give reps a live stock view and train them to always offer an in-stock alternative brand/size/colour before the customer reacts to unavailability.

conversion.title: Move price from 'not discussed' to a clear position early
conversion.evidence: 949 calls (60%) end with price 'not_discussed'; only 141 reach 'accepted'.
conversion.action: Train reps to proactively state pricing and value early in the call instead of deferring, so customers can commit before shopping elsewhere.

conversion.title: Qualify every unknown-segment caller
conversion.evidence: 'Unknown' segment is 519 calls (33%) but wins only 26%, the second-lowest of all segments.
conversion.action: Require reps to ask and log customer type (dealer/fabricator/contractor/end-user) and need in the first minute of the call to tailor the pitch.

conversion.title: Lean into quality/credit conversations where we already win more
conversion.evidence: quality_doubt objections win 31% and credit_terms win 31% — both higher than price_high (28%) or stock (25%).
conversion.action: When price is raised, pivot the conversation toward quality assurance and flexible terms, which the data shows convert better than discount negotiation.

loyalty.title: Consider a formal repeat-buyer recognition programme
loyalty.how: Tag repeat_buyer and bulk_buyer customers in CRM; give them a named contact, priority handling, and periodic check-in calls.
loyalty.why: repeat_buyer appears in 126 calls but loyal_to_us is logged in only 14 — loyalty is present but not being reinforced.

loyalty.title: Proactive rate/stock update broadcasts
loyalty.how: Send scheduled WhatsApp/SMS updates on rates and new stock to known dealers instead of waiting for inbound calls.
loyalty.why: regular_updates is a top need (105 calls) and many customers call repeatedly just to check 'what's the rate today'.

loyalty.title: Dedicated account manager for top dealers
loyalty.how: Assign a single rep to each high-volume dealer account for continuity across orders.
loyalty.why: Dealers are 51% of all calls (811) and have the highest win rate among known segments (39%), showing strong relationship potential.

loyalty.title: Light-touch referral recognition
loyalty.how: Acknowledge and thank customers who refer others with small non-price gestures (e.g., priority service, goodwill items).
loyalty.why: referral behaviour logged in only 13 calls — an under-leveraged but existing source of new business.

loyalty.title: Proactive quality documentation and after-sales check-ins
loyalty.how: Send test certificates/quality assurance notes automatically with large orders; follow up after delivery on satisfaction.
loyalty.why: quality_assurance needed in 69 calls, test_certificate in 12, and quality_doubt is a top-8 objection (61 calls).

loyalty.title: Continue/extend small goodwill gestures for loyal accounts
loyalty.how: Formalise small giveaways (e.g., branded notepads) as a recognised loyalty touch for long-standing customers.
loyalty.why: One call summary shows a loyal customer explicitly requesting more notepads while affirming loyalty despite buying elsewhere.

non_price_benefits.title: Broad multi-brand portfolio under one call
non_price_benefits.why: Competitor brands (JSW, Tata, Pragathi, Asian, Radiance, etc.) are frequently compared within the same call — being able to offer multiple brands is a real differentiator worth highlighting.

non_price_benefits.title: Strong technical guidance on specs and profiles
non_price_benefits.why: technical_advice is the 2nd highest need (228) and several 'went well' calls show reps successfully explaining thickness/profile options, closing the sale.

non_price_benefits.title: Same-day/fast dispatch capability
non_price_benefits.why: Multiple successful calls cite material 'dispatched within minutes' or same-day delivery — this speed should be actively promoted, not just delivered.

non_price_benefits.title: Full accessory range beyond sheets
non_price_benefits.why: Top products include screws (65), welding rods (47), polycarbonate (41) and purlins (25) — positioning as a one-stop supplier adds value beyond sheet price.

non_price_benefits.title: Consistent supply and quality assurance
non_price_benefits.why: consistent_supply (67) and quality_assurance (69) are meaningful needs, and quality_doubt objections convert well (31%) when addressed — proof quality messaging works.

non_price_benefits.title: Customisation (cutting, bends, specific profiles)
non_price_benefits.why: cutting_processing need (58) and multiple calls about bend specs/profile changes show customers value flexibility beyond standard sizes.

top_questions.question: What is the current rate for [product/size]?
top_questions.answer_tip: Give a confident, immediate answer with validity period and confirm in writing via WhatsApp same call — avoid delays that erode trust.

top_questions.question: Can the price be reduced / can you match a competitor's rate?
top_questions.answer_tip: Avoid quick discounting; pivot to quality assurance, consistent supply, and service reliability as the reason for the price, and escalate only if genuinely negotiable.

top_questions.question: Is stock available right now?
top_questions.answer_tip: Check live stock before answering; if unavailable, immediately offer an alternative brand, colour, or size instead of ending the call.

top_questions.question: Will delivery happen by [date/time]?
top_questions.answer_tip: Give a firm, specific commitment and proactively update the customer before the promised time rather than waiting for them to chase.

top_questions.question: Can this be done on credit / can I pay later?
top_questions.answer_tip: Clearly explain current credit policy; for regular dealers, escalate to a manager rather than a flat refusal, since credit_terms objections convert at 31%.

top_questions.question: Why did the price increase suddenly / today?
top_questions.answer_tip: Explain market-linked pricing transparently and, where possible, offer to honour the earlier quote for a short window to preserve trust.

top_questions.question: Can you send the quotation/catalogue on WhatsApp?
top_questions.answer_tip: Always send a written quote or catalogue during or immediately after the call — never leave it verbal-only, since no_quote_sent was flagged in 128 calls.

top_questions.question: Is this the same quality/grade as [competitor brand]?
top_questions.answer_tip: Proactively explain certification, grade, and quality assurance details rather than waiting for the customer to doubt it, as quality_doubt appears in 61 calls.
